title: What is Germany Ausbildung? | SK Immigration Services
description: Germany Ausbildung explained for Pakistani applicants: earn-while-you-train dual system, language needs, contract basics, and how it differs from a university degree.

faqs.question: What is Ausbildung?
faqs.answer: German dual vocational training with a contract and usually a training salary.

faqs.question: Do I need German?
faqs.answer: Almost always yes for workplace Ausbildung.

body:
Answer: Ausbildung is Germany’s dual vocational training system — you train with an employer/school, usually earn a training salary, and work toward a recognized qualification. It is not the same as a tuition-free university degree and almost always needs German language.

Ausbildung vs degree

AusbildungUniversity degree
Core documentTraining contractAdmission letter
Funding proofOften salary in contractOften Sperrkonto
LanguageUsually A2–B1+ (higher for nursing)English and/or German per program

Popular fields

Nursing, hospitality, mechatronics, logistics and more — employer demand varies by region.

Evidence standard before you spend

For anything related to germany, ausbildung, international, keep proofs that a third party can verify: offers on letterhead, bank PDFs with history, attestation receipts, and language results that match the program. Screenshots without context are not a file. If a seller asks you to hide a refusal, change the topic — that is not how SK Immigration works.

  • Offer/contract names match the passport spelling
  • Language rule is printed (IELTS score, MOI, German level, etc.)
  • Funds story matches 3–6 months of statements where missions care about history
  • Attestation order is destination-correct (Apostille vs MOFA paths are not toys)
  • Official mission or university pages were opened the same week you pay

Mistakes we see on “germany ausbildung international” files

  • Believing Ausbildung is available with zero German for nursing/tech roles
  • Paying cash to an unverifiable “German employer agent”
  • Submitting a degree-style SOP for a vocational contract
  • Ignoring recognition/language timelines until the flight week
